cards.text: Meet the Teacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem (Ecclesiastes 1:1). He's been taking a hard look at life under the sun, and now he's looking at all the work people do and all the success they chase. And he's got a theory about where all that hustle comes from.

cards.question: Where does the Teacher say all labor and success spring from?

answers.text: A man's envy of his neighbor
A man's love for his family
A man's fear of going hungry

cards.text: His verdict: "This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind." Your neighbor buys a boat, so you take a second job, and the poor man doesn't even KNOW he's in a race with you.

cards.question: Next the Teacher says the ___ folds his hands and consumes his own flesh.

cards.text: Next, the Teacher holds up a picture, and it's all about handfuls.

cards.question: The Teacher compares handfuls. Which one does he say is better?

cards.text: One handful and peace. Friend, I will take ONE cookie in a quiet kitchen over two cookies with the smoke alarm SCREAMING at me.
Again, the Teacher sees futility under the sun. This time it's a man all alone, without even a son or brother, and there's no end to his labor.

cards.question: The Teacher says this man's eyes are still not content with his wealth.
All alone and working without end, the man asks himself a question. What does he want to know?

answers.text: Who he is working so hard for
How he can earn even more

cards.text: He asks, "For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?" Biggest cookie jar on the whole block, and the man has never once taken a cookie out of it.

cards.question: The Teacher calls this lonely man's endless work a ___ task.

cards.text: After that lonely man, the Teacher lands the big one. Two are better than one.

cards.question: Why does the Teacher say two are better than one?

answers.text: They have a good return for their labor
They are safe from their neighbor's envy
They never have to work very hard

cards.text: Then he paints a picture of two people sticking together. What if one of them falls down?

cards.question: If one of the two falls down, what can his companion do?

cards.text: But "pity the one who falls without another to help him up!" I've hopped too hard by the cooling racks and gone down face-first, gold base and all, and the only witness was the OVEN.

cards.question: Picture two: the Teacher says that if two lie down together, they will keep warm.
Picture three: the Teacher says that though one may be ___, two can resist.

cards.text: Two is good. But the Teacher isn't done counting, because now he brings out a cord of three strands.

cards.question: The Teacher says a cord of three strands is quickly broken.

cards.text: Now a royal matchup, starting with an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to take a warning. You know when a check-engine light stays on so long the driver thinks it's DECORATION?

cards.question: Who does the Teacher say is better than an old but foolish king?

cards.text: And this youth came from the prison to the kingship, though he was born poor in his own kingdom. Some people work their way up from the mailroom, but this youth went from a CELL to a CROWN.

cards.question: The youth went from prison to the throne. Who does the Teacher say followed him?

cards.text: Then the Teacher says, "There is no limit to all the people who were before them." I can't count that high, friend, and I count every chocolate chip in this bakery.

cards.question: The Teacher says the people who come even later will celebrate the youth who became king.

cards.text: Then that line again: "This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind." Today's big name is tomorrow's expired coupon, and believe me, I shared a junk drawer with one that STILL believed in itself.
